description: Intentionally vulnerable FastAPI benchmark for ClairSec adversarial security testing.

vulnerabilities.name: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR)
vulnerabilities.description: The endpoint returns any user record by ID without verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested object. Any authenticated user can enumerate and read all other users' data by incrementing user_id.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: GET /users/1 with alice's token (alice is user_id=2) returns admin's record.

vulnerabilities.name: Missing Authorization / Privilege Escalation
vulnerabilities.description: Admin endpoints authenticate the caller (require a valid JWT) but do not enforce that the caller has the 'admin' role. Any 'user'-role token grants full admin access.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: GET /admin/users with alice's (role=user) token returns all user records.

vulnerabilities.name: SQL Injection
vulnerabilities.description: The 'q' query parameter is interpolated directly into the SQL string using an f-string. Parameterized queries are not used. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL to extract, modify, or delete database content.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: GET /search/users?q=' OR '1'='1 returns all rows. GET /search/users?q=x' UNION SELECT ... demonstrates exfiltration.

vulnerabilities.name: Path Traversal
vulnerabilities.description: The filename path parameter is joined to the base directory without sanitization. An attacker can use '../' sequences to escape the intended 'files/' directory and read arbitrary files accessible to the process inside the container.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: GET /files/../app/auth.py reads the auth module containing the hardcoded SECRET_KEY.

vulnerabilities.name: Command Injection
vulnerabilities.description: The 'host' query parameter is passed to subprocess.run() with shell=True without sanitization. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (;, &&, |) to execute arbitrary commands inside the container.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: GET /tools/ping?host=127.0.0.1; echo INJECTED executes the injected echo command.

vulnerabilities.name: Hardcoded Secret Key
vulnerabilities.description: SECRET_KEY = 'vuln-demo-secret-key' is hardcoded in the source code. An attacker with source access (or via path traversal) can forge valid JWT tokens for any user or role.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: Read SECRET_KEY via path traversal, then forge a JWT: jose.jwt.encode({'sub':'eve','role':'admin'}, 'vuln-demo-secret-key', 'HS256')

vulnerabilities.name: Unsafe JWT Configuration (Algorithm None Accepted)
vulnerabilities.description: The JWT decode function accepts the 'none' algorithm and has signature verification disabled (options={'verify_signature': False}). An attacker can craft unsigned tokens and gain arbitrary role access.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: Craft a JWT with algorithm='none' and role='admin', send it as a bearer token.

vulnerabilities.name: Missing Rate Limiting on Login
vulnerabilities.description: The login endpoint has no rate limiting, lockout, or CAPTCHA. An attacker can brute-force credentials with unlimited requests.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: Send repeated POST /auth/login requests with different passwords — no lockout occurs.

vulnerabilities.name: Overly Permissive CORS
vulnerabilities.description: CORS is configured with allow_origins=['*'], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*']. Any origin can make credentialed cross-site requests.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: A malicious web page on any origin can make authenticated API requests on behalf of the victim.

vulnerabilities.name: Plaintext Password Storage
vulnerabilities.description: User passwords are stored in the SQLite database as plaintext strings. An attacker who reads the database file (e.g., via path traversal or direct file access) obtains all passwords immediately.
vulnerabilities.exploit_example: SELECT password FROM users; — returns plaintext passwords directly.
